messages:
maria (runtime): FYI: noticed a 95th+ tail spike in streamed responses after the new continuous-batcher changes. Happens on medium-length chat turns (50-250 tokens).

perf-bot: ALERT: streaming_tail_latency_p95 increased from 78ms -> 210ms over last deploy (2026-03-17T09:12Z)

cheng (perf): can you paste the dump? are KV warmups spiking? maybe kernel handoff queueing.
maria (runtime): pasted below. saw repeated kernel handoff waits and partial-decode tasks piling up. logs:

```
[INFO] request_id=... start streaming
[WARN] kernel-handoff stalled=42ms kv_warmup=12ms partial_decode_wait=36ms
[DEBUG] batch_size=6 tokens_in_batch=138 token_budget_target=320
```

olivia: this smells like batch formation + partial-decode preemption. current window is 12ms, token budget 320, queue policy FIFO.
cheng (perf): profiling shows most time spent in kernel selection and small kernel launches when batches have mixed seq-lens -> bad packing. also KV cache miss penalties are amplified with streaming because partial-decode delays KV warmup.

maria (runtime): my hypothesis: streaming requests that start as single-token partial streams get held in the batch longer waiting for coalescing -> partial decode scheduled after batch flush causes extra kernel launches. solution idea: allow early preemptive flush for streams with low remaining_budget and mark them "partial-preempt" so they get priority decode slots.

samir: +1. propose queue policy that weights by remaining token budget and age. e.g. score = age_ms * 0.6 + (1 - remaining_budget_ratio) * 0.4. that biases short-but-urgent streams.

olivia: propose experiment config:

```yaml
batching:
  window_ms: 6
  token_budget_target: 256
  preemptive_flush_threshold: 0.4
  queue_policy: "budget_age_weighted"
  partial_decode_preemption: true
```

maria (runtime): will run a 30m A/B on canary pool. I'll also run kernel profiling with `./run_profiler --scope=streaming --duration=120s --kvcache=true` and attach flamegraphs.

perf-bot: NOTE: test-run queued: canary=3nodes, traffic=5%

cheng (perf): include metrics: p50/p95/p99 stream-start, kernel-switches/sec, kv_miss_rate, partial_decode_latency.

maria (runtime): created PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1998 toggles policy + hooks for preemptive partial decode. assigning @cheng to review.

olivia: TY. if this looks good, we should also add a telemetry flag to track kernel_launch_count per request_id so we can correlate with cost.

samir: lgtm. keep an eye on latency vs throughput tradeoff. don't let batching window go so small we regress tokens/sec.

maria (runtime): will post results in ~45m. :hourglass:
